title: Every Tauri command carries an actor argument (human or agent)
context: Alternative approaches: no actor tracking; infer from caller context; use permission tokens.
decision: Every Tauri command carries an `actor` argument in the payload, holding either `human` or `agent`. The shell supplies an actor token on every command call. Commands that gate by actor (e.g., the accept transition) read this field and enforce the gate at the command boundary.
consequences: Commands can make policy decisions based on actor type; the accept transition (human-only) is enforced in the Tauri layer, not the UI layer; agent impersonation attempts fail at the boundary; the field is always present and always correct (supplied by shell, not caller).
